intermediateResults.title: Exact product additivity of the averaged relaxed-UV scalar
intermediateResults.statement: For a finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channel W, let t_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)-I_p(X;Z), let C denote the upper concave envelope on the input simplex, define A_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)+C[-t_W](p) and D_W(p)=I_p(X;Z)+C[t_W](p), and set B_avg(W)=sup_p (A_W(p)+D_W(p))/2. For arbitrary finite-alphabet DMBCs W_1 and W_2, B_avg(W_1×W_2)=B_avg(W_1)+B_avg(W_2). The product-channel input prior may be correlated across factors, and the envelope auxiliary may be joint across factors.
scopeQualifications: No objective execution attestations were supplied; scripts and hash statements are merely corroborative, while the theorem is supported by the analytic proof.
The general product-additivity argument is established internally and does not require the declared BSSC dependency.

intermediateResults.title: Receiver-skew symmetry bridge and exact BSSC product value
intermediateResults.statement: With A_W and D_W as in result-uv-average-product-additivity, define B_br(W)=sup_p min{A_W(p),D_W(p)}. If a finite-alphabet DMBC has an involutive input relabeling that exchanges its two receivers, then B_br(W)=B_avg(W), and the optimization may be restricted to input laws invariant under that involution. Finite products preserve this receiver-skew symmetry, so B_br and B_avg are both exactly additive on arbitrary finite products of such channels. For the half-skew BSSC P, whose unique invariant binary input law is the fair prior, the sharp one-letter BSSC posterior-support result gives, for every finite n≥1, B_br(P^{×n})=B_avg(P^{×n})=n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4), with normalized value 0.3725562489182657… bits per channel use.
scopeQualifications: Branchwise equality is established only under receiver-exchanging involutive input symmetry; no corresponding claim is made for nonsymmetric channels.
No objective execution attestations were supplied; scripts and hash statements are merely corroborative, while the theorem is supported by the analytic proof.
